summary.title: Dense-TSNet: Dense Connected Two-Stage Structure for Ultra-Lightweight Speech Enhancement
summary.authors: Zizhen Lin, Yuanle Li, Junyu Wang, Ruili Li
summary.executive_summary: This paper introduces Dense-TSNet, an ultra-lightweight speech enhancement network designed for resource-constrained edge devices. The authors address the limitations of existing deep neural networks, which often suffer from high complexity and uneven loss landscapes in narrow architectures. Dense-TSNet employs a novel Dense Two-Stage (Dense-TS) architecture that replaces dilated convolutions with densely connected Two-Stage modules to ensure smoother loss landscapes and better convergence in later training stages. A key component is the Multi-View Gaze Block (MVGB), which integrates global, channel, and local feature extraction using only convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for efficiency. The study also investigates loss functions, demonstrating that a Consistency Magnitude Loss yields superior perceptual quality compared to Metric Loss, which can introduce distortions. Evaluated on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset, Dense-TSNet achieves a PESQ score of 3.05 with only 14K parameters and 356M MACs, outperforming several state-of-the-art lightweight methods while maintaining a compact footprint suitable for deployment on smartphones and cameras.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper introduces Dense-TSNet, an ultra-lightweight speech enhancement network designed for resource-constrained edge devices. The authors address the limitations of existing deep neural networks, which often suffer from high complexity and uneven loss landscapes in narrow architectures. Dense-TSNet employs a novel Dense Two-Stage (Dense-TS) architecture that replaces dilated convolutions with densely connected Two-Stage modules to ensure smoother loss landscapes and better convergence in later training stages. A key component is the Multi-View Gaze Block (MVGB), which integrates global, channel, and local feature extraction using only convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for efficiency. The study also investigates loss functions, demonstrating that a Consistency Magnitude Loss yields superior perceptual quality compared to Metric Loss, which can introduce distortions. Evaluated on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset, Dense-TSNet achieves a PESQ score of 3.05 with only 14K parameters and 356M MACs, outperforming several state-of-the-art lightweight methods while maintaining a compact footprint suitable for deployment on smartphones and cameras.

Research Context
Speech enhancement is vital for noisy environments but current models are too complex. Recent Two-Stage architectures improve feature extraction but struggle with narrow models. Advanced operators like Transformers lack the efficiency of CNNs for real-world deployment. There is a significant gap in research for single-channel models with around 10k parameters.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can a Dense Two-Stage architecture resolve convergence issues in ultra-lightweight networks? Does a Multi-View Gaze Block enhance feature extraction using only CNNs? Does Consistency Magnitude Loss outperform Metric Loss for perceptual quality in lightweight models? Can a model achieve SOTA performance with approximately 10k parameters?

Methodological Details
The study utilized the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset for high-fidelity utterances. Speech samples were segmented into two-second intervals for processing. An FFT size of 400, window length of 400, and hop length of 100 were employed. Training was conducted with a batch size of 2 using the AdamW optimizer. The training process was carried out for up to 1,000,000 steps. The model inputs only the magnitude spectrum derived from the complex spectrum. The classic Two-Stage architecture uses a channel count of 64 for robust feature fusion. The proposed Dense-TSNet has a narrow architecture with 4 channels. The Dense-TS structure replaces dilated convolutions with Two-Stage modules. The Multi-View Gaze Block consists of Large Kernel Extractor, Learnable-Sigmoid Gate, and Channel Attention.

Procedures And Architectures
The network reshapes spectral feature maps to handle temporal and frequency dependencies. Input channels to the i-th Two-Stage layer are calculated as dense channel times i plus one. Output channels from the adjust convolutional layer are set to the dense channel count. The TS-MVGB output is a serial connection of time-MVGB and freq-MVGB. The final output combines the last skip connection with the input using a weight of 0.2. An extra residual connection is added beyond dense connections. Features undergo L-Sigmoid activation and 1x1 convolution to decode the magnitude spectrum mask. The Large Kernel Extractor uses pointwise convolutions, Simple Gate, large kernel depthwise convolutions, and HardSwish. Channel Attention reallocates weights to focus on important channels. The Learnable-Sigmoid Gate focuses on modeling local information within the feature map.

Key Results
Dense-TSNet achieves a PESQ score of 3.05 on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset. The model achieves CSIG, CBAK, and COVL scores of 4.51, 3.58, and 3.86 respectively. The model has a parameter count of 14K and MACs of 356M. Dense-TSNet outperforms the Classic TS structure in later training stages. Removing the Large Kernel Extractor drops the PESQ score to 2.79. Removing the Channel Attention drops the PESQ score to 2.86. Removing the Learnable-Sigmoid Gate drops the PESQ score to 2.97. Removing Consistency Loss drops the PESQ score to 2.96. Using Metric Loss with P=200 introduces pseudohallucination distortion. Training fails when the Metric Loss weight ratio P is set to 400.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Dense connections provide a smoother loss landscape for narrow models. The Multi-View Gaze Block effectively captures global, channel, and local perspectives. Consistency Magnitude Loss is preferred over Metric Loss for perceptual quality. Metric Loss can lead to increased errors in amplitude and phase spectra. The proposed architecture enables deployment in resource-constrained environments.

Contradictions And Limitations
The paper notes that future work will explore further model compression. Metric Loss was found to cause training failure at high weight ratios. The study relies on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset, limiting generalizability to other noise types.

Claims
Dense-TSNet achieves state-of-the-art performance with an ultra-lightweight footprint of 14K parameters. The model has a parameter count of 14K and MACs of 356M. It outperforms Classic TS and other lightweight algorithms in Table I.  This enables deployment on edge devices like smartphones.
The Consistency Magnitude Loss is superior to Metric Loss for perceptual quality in lightweight models. Metric Loss may negatively impact subjective perception. Pseudohallucination distortion occurs at P=200 with Metric Loss. Metric Loss increases PESQ scores when P is small (e.g., P=1). Objective metrics may not align with subjective perception in lightweight networks.

Data And Code Availability
Source codes will be released after paper acceptance. Audio samples can be found at the provided GitHub link.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Ablation on LKE shows a significant drop in PESQ from 3.05 to 2.79. Ablation on CA shows a drop in PESQ from 3.05 to 2.86. Ablation on LSG shows a drop in PESQ from 3.05 to 2.97. Ablation on Consistency Loss shows a drop in PESQ from 3.05 to 2.96. Training fails when Metric Loss weight ratio P is set to 400.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 illustrates the overall architecture of Classic Two-Stage and Dense-TS. Figure 2 details the internal components of the LKE, LSG, and CA. Figure 3 shows the training criteria of the proposed Dense-TSNet. Figure 4 displays the training curves for Dense-TS and Classic-TS. Table I compares performance with other methods on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset. Table II presents ablation study results on the VoiceBank+DEMAND Dataset. Table III studies the effect of different loss functions.

Three Takeaways
Dense-TSNet achieves SOTA performance with only 14K parameters. The Dense-TS architecture ensures smoother loss landscapes for narrow models. Future work will focus on further compressing the model size.
